T-014.title: Test APIR authenticated-count plus authenticated-point-query composition for OMR completeness
T-014.description: Assess a conditional route for OMR completeness using APIR authenticated predicate COUNT plus authenticated private point queries. Determine whether FSS can express the exact OMR signal-membership predicate and any index-range/subrange counts; how the client discovers the matching indices rather than merely learning their number; whether count and point answers bind to one immutable database snapshot; what a malicious detector can omit or equivocate about; and how output cardinality, access count, timing and communication volume leak. Include false positives, 32-bit signal collisions, candidate-capacity overflow, admission receipts and sender-manifest closure. Do not assume that a count plus arbitrary point queries enumerates the matches.
T-014.next_action: Read the pinned APIR artifact code at commit 7a7f2041bc1e0907ef089f8e8e55252ef7f18e0f (predicate client/server, FSS implementation, query representation and point-query path) alongside SRC-054. Formalise a candidate count-to-index-discovery procedure or reject the route if it requires an O(N) scan, leaks the matching indices/cardinality, or cannot bind all answers to one immutable snapshot. Compare any candidate against SRC-056–SRC-060 and the OMR/UnifOMR capacity boundary. No build/test or construction claim without evidence.
T-014.completion_rule: A source-grounded feasibility assessment states whether the OMR predicate is expressible in APIR FSS; how all matching indices are found; whether count and point answers share one authenticated snapshot; soundness/completeness against a malicious detector; leakage and cost; collision/false-positive/overflow handling; and admission/manifest limitations. Deliver either a defensible construction outline or a negative feasibility result. No proof, implementation or benchmark claim without evidence.
blockers: Full SRC-056 APIR-range PDF and SRC-059 VPRQ technical paper remain inaccessible; retain partial-source status and avoid novelty claims.
APIR artifact is source-inspected only; no build, test, benchmark or independent security review has been performed.
